Stack.label: The stack
Stack.title: The tools behind those products.
Stack.lede: Nothing here is new to Divine — every one of these has already carried something of his into production, which is what makes a delivery date worth quoting.

bullets.b1: Became the primary backend engineer for a multi-tenant faith-community platform used by churches and ministries (giving, community, messaging) — the person new features and cross-team backend issues route to, across 15+ services.
bullets.b2: Protected recurring giving and subscription revenue from silent failures: fixed a renewal race that could drop active subscriptions mid-payment, and added recovery that reconciles failed renewals without ever double-charging donors.
bullets.b3: Secured customer organizations' admin controls against takeover — rebuilt role authorization across every service and closed a path where non-admins could grant themselves admin rights.
bullets.b4: Made platform data trustworthy under load: a user action like a deletion or role change now propagates once and correctly across every service, even when events are retried or arrive out of order.

bullets.b1: Made a crowdfunding platform's core "all-or-nothing" promise real: re-architected money flow so backer funds are held in escrow and released to creators only when a campaign hits its goal — otherwise every backer is automatically refunded — protecting both sides of the transaction.
bullets.b2: Eliminated a bug that double-counted campaign totals and tax figures — reworked payment processing so a duplicate or retried provider notification can never be counted twice, verified under concurrent load.
bullets.b3: Built the compliance controls a money-moving product needs to operate legally: a tamper-proof audit trail, anti-money-laundering caps, and automated tax-threshold reporting.
bullets.b4: Made automated trading safe on a custodial trading platform — a crash-safe execution engine with built-in guardrails (spending caps, kill-switches, auto-pause) and hardware-key-protected withdrawals, so trades can't run away or exceed set limits.

bullets.b1: Founded and lead a senior software agency — 10+ production platforms shipped across fintech, remittance, ticketing, and education, including 5 apps published to the App Store and Play Store.
bullets.b2: Built a cross-border remittance app (live on both stores, 5 corridors into Central Africa) that guarantees senders the exact rate they saw — the exchange rate is locked at submission with money-safe decimal handling and duplicate-transfer protection, so diaspora transfers land correct to the last franc.
bullets.b3: Authored stateledger, an open-source payment state-machine library for Node/TypeScript (3 packages on npm) — the reliable equivalent the Node ecosystem was missing for handling payment workflows.
bullets.b4: Also shipped a pan-African admissions platform letting students apply and pay by mobile money across 10 countries without traveling to campus; a mobile-money event-ticketing platform with fraud-resistant QR tickets; and PulseLab, a real-time webhook debugger.

bullets.b1: Gave a diaspora dating app a reliable foundation to scale on — led its migration from MongoDB to PostgreSQL, restructuring the entire data model (33 models, 150+ endpoints) for enforceable integrity.
bullets.b2: Stopped subscription revenue leaking from forged or unverified receipts by adding cryptographic verification across Apple, Google, and card payments.
bullets.b3: Rebuilt match discovery on a location-aware scoring engine; the product reached 1,000+ users in its first month.

bullets.b1: Rebuilt AECO Education and Saint Louis University's digital presence (30% engagement lift) and built the student-application system that grew into a pan-African admissions platform.
Led a team of 3 engineers and 10 interns; owned technical scoping of all incoming projects.
bullets.b2: Built the digital platform for a 5-company conglomerate that generated 3M FCFA in its first two months and drove a 30% annual revenue increase.
bullets.b3: Built RHIIBMS, a school-management system that cut admission processing by weeks with 100% budget-calculation accuracy.

hero.label: About
hero.title: Seven years of making the hard parts behave.

story.p1: Enow Divine is a senior software engineer based in <mark>{location}</mark>, building the payment and correctness layers behind fintech, remittance and SaaS products used across the US, Europe and Africa. He started freelancing in 2018 and formalized it into a small studio, SaaS Simplified, shortly after.
story.p2: His specialty is <mark>payment systems and money-movement correctness</mark> — idempotent webhooks, decimal-safe money math, race-free inventory, cryptographic receipt verification, escrow flows, audit trails. In plain terms: the work that decides whether your customers get charged twice, and whether your finance team can trust the numbers. He is equally comfortable across the stack — React, Next.js, React Native — when a project calls for it.
story.p3: He has shipped 10+ production platforms across fintech, remittance, ticketing and education — including 5 apps published to the App Store and Play Store — and authored <mark>stateledger</mark>, an open-source payment state-machine library for Node/TypeScript. Today he splits his time between full-time US backend work and running SaaS Simplified, the engineering studio he founded.
story.p4: Clients tend to be founders and small teams who have something that has to work the first time — money moving, users waiting, a launch date that will not move.

payments.name: Payment systems
payments.description: For fintech products, marketplaces, and any platform moving money between two sides. Cards, mobile money, escrow, subscriptions — the parts that have to be right the first time.
payments.howItStarts: A discovery call maps your money flow — sources, custody points, exits — and names the risky joints: duplicate processing, race conditions, reconciliation gaps. A fixed proposal follows within a few days.

process.p1: Map the money flow: sources, custody points, exits
process.p2: Choose the provider stack (Stripe, Paystack, MTN/Orange Mobile Money, Fapshi)
process.p3: Design idempotent processing and escrow rules
process.p4: Build the audit trail before shipping anything else
process.p5: Wire compliance hooks: transaction limits, KYC, threshold reporting
process.p6: Load-test the concurrency story before go-live

deliverables.d1: Payment processing service in your codebase, integrated with your provider(s)
deliverables.d2: A state machine for every money-movement flow, tested against duplicates and races
deliverables.d3: Reconciliation dashboard or CLI for your finance and ops team
deliverables.d4: Runbook for the common failure modes: duplicate webhook, provider outage, partial refund
deliverables.d5: Written architecture doc for whoever maintains it next

process.p1: Define the positioning, the audience, and the primary conversion action
process.p2: Sitemap and wireframe review before any design work
process.p3: Build page by page, with weekly demos
process.p4: SEO and performance instrumentation baked in, not bolted on
process.p5: Contact form wired to your inbox, analytics live
process.p6: Deploy and hand over to your team

deliverables.d1: Live site on your own domain (Vercel or your infrastructure)
deliverables.d2: A fully editable Next.js and Tailwind codebase in your repo

ai.name: AI integrations
ai.description: For teams adding real LLM features to their product — not chatbot demos, but production workflows with cost caps and fallbacks.
ai.howItStarts: Discovery on the use case, your latency and cost constraints, and — most importantly — where AI actually helps versus where a plain form field would do the job better.

process.p1: Define the use case and agree what a correct output looks like
process.p2: Model selection (OpenAI, Anthropic, Groq) with real cost analysis
process.p3: Prompt design plus a small evaluation harness, so iteration is confident
process.p4: Streaming UX and fallback logic for model outages
process.p5: A retrieval pipeline if the feature needs one (pgvector or a dedicated embeddings DB)
process.p6: Cost and rate-limit guardrails before any of it reaches real users

deliverables.d1: The AI feature integrated in your codebase, with streaming UX
deliverables.d2: Prompt library and evaluation set, so your team can keep iterating
deliverables.d4: Fallback logic for model outages and rate limits
deliverables.d5: Deployment and observability for the AI-specific paths
deliverables.d6: A doc explaining the prompt design decisions and how to change them

faq.label: Common questions
faq.title: Before you write.
faq.lede: Anything not answered here is worth asking on the intake call — it is free, and it is the fastest way to find out whether this is a fit.

scope.q: Does Divine handle both building and advising?
scope.a: Yes. Most engagements are build work — payment systems, SaaS, mobile, marketing sites, AI features. He also takes advisory-only work when a team just needs a second opinion or an ongoing brain to bounce things off.

advisoryToBuild.q: Can advisory turn into a full build?
advisoryToBuild.a: Yes. If an advisory engagement surfaces work you want done, it gets scoped separately and SaaS Simplified takes it on. Advisory and build are always billed separately — there is never upsell pressure inside the advisory hours.

who.a: Divine, as the senior engineer accountable for the engagement. Larger builds are delivered through SaaS Simplified, the agency he founded in 2018, and the scope says up front who is involved.

nda.a: Yes. Send yours and it gets reviewed; if you do not have one, there is a short mutual NDA ready to share.

speed.a: Most engagements kick off within a week of signature. Larger builds can take longer to schedule, and you will hear that on the intake call rather than after signing.

capacity.a: A small number, deliberately, so every client gets real senior attention rather than shared time. If there is no capacity, you will be told on the intake call and offered a start date.
